# Wave028 — full-Y normalization is a query-weight contrast

Independent FIRST; peer028 unread. **Zero new mechanisms/IDs:** refine existing TLAB008/006 and loss-selection03/review01–03, which already identify candidate-IDCG query reweighting. HYP043/044/075/076 remain unallocated. Public reproduction stays the main priority; no B/W/018 recipe,CI,tolerance or authority changes.

**Mechanism.** For binary targets let I(m)=Σ[r=1..min(20,m)]1/log2(r+1), m=|Yq| and c=|Yq∩Cq|. With m,c>0, wq=I(c)/I(m) and NDCGfull=wq·NDCGC for every permutation of the same C. Therefore any identical pair-swap numerator divided by full IDCG equals wq times its candidate-normalized counterpart. Under a linear lambda construction, both gradient and Hessian coefficients scale by wq. This is normalization, not recovery of unreachable targets or additional predictive information.

**Primary limits.** LambdaLoss connects metric-dependent pair weights to surrogates; its benchmark gains do not establish our sparse-purchase benefit. [Wang et al.,CIKM2018,Eq6/§6.2](https://marc.najork.org/papers/cikm2018.pdf) LightGBM v4.6.0 builds IDCG from candidate labels, then optionally applies score-distance adjustment and log2(1+Σλ)/Σλ normalization; row weights are applied afterward. Thus direct denominator replacement and post-hoc wq are generally unequal with nonlinear normalization. Set normalization false in both conceptual arms, or specify the actual transformed objective. Native truncation/pair numerators also need separate scrutiny; normalizer alignment alone does not make native loss exact NDCG20. [Pinned author code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/LightGBM/v4.6.0/src/objective/rank_objective.hpp)

**Prediction / counterexample.** Identical one-positive/one-negative candidate lists with fullY sizes1 and2 have identical candidate-normalized lambdas but full-Y coefficient ratio1/(1+1/log2(3)). If c=m, or both exceed20, wq=1 and this mechanism disappears. If c=0, all candidate labels are zero: pairwise signal stays zero despite fullY-positive evaluation. EmptyC,zeroY,singleton/all-positive groups remain in manifests; no target insertion or query filtering follows. Reweighting may hurt finite-model sharing; matching metric units guarantees no quality improvement.

**Strong control.** Compare the same lambda learner, features,Q/C,eligible-pair law,capacity,initial scores,iteration/seed budget and normalization setting. Use a uniform coefficient with the same total informative-query weight as wq to separate relative weighting from global mass/regularization. Frozen strong B is a benchmark; changing learner/loss versus B alone cannot identify this correction. Mature full trainY supplies weights before fit, never features, sampler/query selection or future metadata.

**Nearest finite UNRUN experiment / cost.** Six invented queries,≤32 candidate rows,≤48 target pairs,three score vectors and≤6000 pair-coefficient checks: direct full-IDCG versus candidate-IDCG×w, plus the nonlinear-normalization counterexample,zero support and20/21 boundary. First unequal linear coefficient rejects the proposed equivalence. Cap15CPU/30wall seconds/128MiB including construction,oracle,sorting,Hessian checks and failures;0 real scans/fits/predictions. No experiment ran. Real weight preparation/training/validation costs remain unmeasured and ungranted.

**Task1 benefit.** Clarifies which query weighting a future objective tests. No new quality trial or mandatory gate; opened final is not fresh validation. Public-route completion takes priority.

# Wave028 FIRST — full-Y loss alignment

**Disposition:** zero new IDs; refine TLAB006/TLAB008 and own wave008 coverage-oracle argument. Optional future research; no current recipe, cohort, CI, tolerance, or gate changes.

**Mechanism.** Let m=|Yq|, h=|Yq∩Cq| and D(k)=Σ[j=1..min(20,k)]1/log₂(j+1). For h>0, NDCGfull=rq·NDCGC, rq=D(h)/D(m). Thus a hypothetical loss whose pair coefficients are linear in ΔNDCGC can use rq to reproduce full-IDCG coefficients. This is an algebraic surrogate-weight adaptation, not a quality claim. Current B/W Logloss has no IDCG normalization; existing PairLogit uses 1/(p·n), not ΔNDCG. Clipping, sampling, and per-query renormalization require separate inspection.[1]

**Prediction/counterexample.** Fix C={a,b}, a positive, b observed nonpositive. Query A has fullY={a}; B has fullY={a,z}, z outside C. Moving a from rank2 to rank1 gives equal shortlist improvements δ=1−1/log₂3, but full improvements δ and δ/(1+1/log₂3). Shortlist normalization relatively overweights B by 1+1/log₂3. Conversely, if every informative query has equal rq, matched global weight normalization removes the relative allocation difference. No weighting retrieves z: the full metric ceiling remains D(h)/D(m). Off-C targets are never negatives.

**Nearest finite UNRUN experiment.** A four-query literal specification: A/B above; C with fullY={z}; D with empty mature fullY. Each has the same two-item C. Compare two fixed rank orders, then analytically compare pair coefficients under shortlist versus full normalization. C has constant-zero full NDCG and no positive-negative ranking pairs; D has undefined conditional metric. Preserve both in their original evaluation domains.[2] Any dropped C, fabricated positive, or undefined-ratio weight fails the control.

**Strong control/task1 benefit.** A later authorized trained contrast must keep Q/C/features, mature labels, pair-support masks, seeds, iterations and pair enumeration identical; alter only the declared coefficient multiplier, with a common global mass convention. Keep zero-pair groups identically handled. Comparing a new listwise loss against current Logloss would confound support and objective. This prevents automatic feature selection from miscrediting coverage-dependent query weighting as feature discovery. No prediction feature or query selection may depend on rq; full label windows must mature before fit.

**Cost/negative outcome.** Literal scope: 4 Q, 8 C rows, 4 target rows, 16 returned positions, 2 eligible pairs, zero fits. Future preparation costs O(Σ(|Y|+|C|)) membership work plus existing O(Σh(|C|−h)) pairs and O(Q) weight state; both fits, full source/authentication, checkpoints, scoring and failed attempts are charged. No grant. A failed identity falsifies implementation; no prospective gain or harm leaves this deferred, without retuning current final.
